checkpoints.description: [1/5] Data layer: add paper tags and study_type (schema v2 with v1 migration), deterministic study-type inference, and literature search matching tags, words and sentences, with failing-first tests; [2/5] propagate fields through ingest, discovery and manual paper add; [3/5] Web Studio literature search panel (tag chips, word/sentence search, study-type filter) and study-type labels on paper graph nodes; [4/5] README, ADR and knowledge-map refresh; [5/5] Phase 4 gates and delivery

impact_assessment.why: User asked for search by tags, words or sentences in the literature area and for study type to appear on graph points, so literature discovery/curation must expose searchable metadata and graph nodes must carry study-type context.
impact_assessment.benefits: Researchers can find papers in the literature list by keyword phrase, exact sentence, generated/user tags and study type; graph nodes identify the kind of study behind each paper; AI agents receive the same metadata through the shared repository.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: paper payloads gain two fields, existing v1 databases must migrate without data loss, CLI/MCP/web payloads stay backward-compatible; dependency: standard library only, no new packages; concurrency: schema migration runs once under SQLite's existing connection/busy timeout, no background writers; state: tags/study_type persist in SQLite and JSONL snapshots, inference is deterministic and leaves explicit values untouched.
impact_assessment.mitigation: add columns through an idempotent v1->v2 migration with a backup-free ADD COLUMN path, keep defaults empty so old snapshots import, cover migration and search in unit tests, and run the full project gates before committing.

[1/5] Analysis: detect and link related findings (claims) sharing a research question or at least two domain keywords, excluding opposing stances and existing links, capped at three per claim, deterministic and idempotent with explanatory notes; auto-link new claims during extraction and catch up existing graphs through analyze --auto-link, with failing-first tests. [2/5] AI navigation: related_findings(target, limit) over claims, papers and questions with relation reasons and next-hop refs, plus the CLI related command and the MCP related_findings tool. [3/5] Web map: draw edges by kind with distinct colors and dashes, add a legend, and add a Connect Findings action backed by a JSON endpoint. [4/5] README, ADR-009 and codebase map. [5/5] Phase 4 gates, checklist record and commit.

impact_assessment.why: The user asked that related findings connect on the map and that an AI agent can navigate those connections easily; today claims only link to questions, so related findings stay isolated and agents must guess relevance.
impact_assessment.benefits: The map becomes a connected evidence web instead of star-shaped question hubs; an agent can walk from a finding to related, supporting or contradicting findings with the reason and the next-hop reference in one bounded call.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: extraction edge payloads grow when related links are created, and CLI/MCP gain new surfaces; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: links are added through the existing SQLite connection with the same commit pattern and no background writers; state: related edges persist in SQLite and snapshots, so linking must be idempotent and bounded to avoid duplicate or runaway edges.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use deterministic pair ordering and sorted identifiers, skip pairs that already share any claim-to-claim edge, exclude opposing stances owned by contradiction detection, cap links per claim, explain each edge in its note, and cover thresholds, idempotency, extraction, CLI, MCP, web and map rendering with tests before the gates.

Task 'lattice-related-findings-navigation' completed successfully.

[1/5] New lattice.context module: token-budgeted compact views for AI agents (compact_search, compact_related, compact_subgraph, outline) with truncation, omitted counts and a hard budget floor; failing-first tests. [2/5] MCP: read tools search, related_findings and subgraph return compact budgeted payloads with tokens arguments, plus a new outline tool for cheap orientation; get_entity stays the full drill-down; tests. [3/5] CLI: outline command and tokens options on search, related and subgraph, with JSON output using the compact views; tests. [4/5] README, ADR-010 and codebase map. [5/5] Phase 4 gates, checklist record and commit.

impact_assessment.why: AI clients currently receive full abstracts, duplicated edge endpoint details and untruncated claim text, so a handful of read calls can consume thousands of tokens; the user wants RLM-style navigation where an agent peeks at a cheap index and expands only the handles it needs.
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent can orient with a small outline, then search or expand compact refs under an explicit token budget, reporting omitted items instead of silently overflowing; full text is paid for only through get_entity on a chosen ref.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: MCP payloads for search, subgraph and related_findings become compact and gain tokens arguments, while CLI gains commands and flags; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only views over existing queries; state: no schema or persistence change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build the compact views as pure functions over existing repository payloads, keep the web UI and human CLI defaults on full data, retain refs on every item so nothing becomes unreachable, report omitted counts, floor the budget, and pin shapes, truncation and omission behavior in tests before the gates.

[3/4] Web Research Studio UI: Corpus Outline drawer/modal, 1-click clipboard copy buttons for synthesis Markdown/BibTeX, and BibTeX download actions. [4/4] Verification, ADR-011, README, codebase map refresh, and delivery gates.

impact_assessment.why: Researchers need quick visual orientation through a Corpus Outline drawer, standard BibTeX bibliography export for paper writing, and 1-click synthesis copying in the Web Studio.
impact_assessment.benefits: Enables direct export of entire or filtered literature sets into BibTeX for LaTeX reference managers, exposes token-frugal graph outlines directly in the web UI, and streamlines human synthesis workflows with instant clipboard copies.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CLI export gains optional --format flag while keeping JSONL default backward-compatible; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only exports over SQLite; state: atomic file writing for exports.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Default to JSONL if format is omitted unless filename ends in .bib/.bibtex, keep SQLite read transactions short, test CLI, web API and UI handlers with sub-second unit tests before Phase 4 gates.

[1/2] Add start.py launcher with companion start.bat and start.sh for 1-click startup, and tests in test_cli.py. [2/2] Update README, refresh codebase map, and run Phase 4 delivery gates.

impact_assessment.why: Users need a single intuitive start file (start.py, start.bat, start.sh) to launch the Lattice Research Studio in browser without having to remember the full module syntax.
impact_assessment.benefits: Allows 1-click double-click startup on Windows, instant terminal launch via python start.py or ./start.sh, and transparent forwarding of custom CLI arguments.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing python -m lattice and lattice CLI entrypoints remain unchanged; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Delegate all execution to existing lattice.cli.main(), keep start.py self-contained, and test default and forwarded invocations in test_cli.py.
